title: Choose the visual world for TuneTracker 2.0
question: Your brief pins the palette (deep navy, electric blue, indigo, controlled violet, neon logo). These directions decide the system and composition inside it. The roll assigned Liner Notes.

options.label: Liner Notes
options.lineage: album credits booklets and tracklist sleeves — 'Produced by · Mixed by · Mastered by'
options.thesis: Every project reads like the credits page of the record it will become: numbered tracklists, role-and-name credits, durations, BPM and key set like sleeve type, lit by the logo's neon on a midnight-navy booklet.
materials: neon gradient as the one light source
options.viewport: Landing opens on the logo's glow behind a credits-sheet hero: 'TuneTracker 2.0 — Create · Collaborate · Share' set like an album title, with the real product's board shown as the record's tracklist; Get Started is the primary action, Learn More scrolls to the claim/proof sections.
options.risk: If the credits typography is set timidly it collapses into a generic dark SaaS page with a gradient sticker.

raised.raise: Every marketing claim is immediately followed by a real interface fragment proving it (board, task sheet, player) — no abstract feature cards.
Unlit states are designed as deliberately as lit ones: empty columns, empty feed and no-project states are composed credit slots, not apologies.
Only the edge that moves takes colour: a dragged card and its drop slot light up; everything at rest stays in the navy frame.
One strict numeric voice: BPM, key, durations, counts and dates all in tabular monospaced figures.

options.label: After Hours
options.lineage: the blueprint poster itself — a studio at 2am, monitors and LEDs glowing in the dark
options.thesis: The app as a dark room lit only by its work: glassy layered panels, ambient violet bloom, glowing waveform accents, exactly the poster's mood.
options.viewport: Centred neon logo and headline over a glowing laptop-style product shot, feature row beneath.
options.risk: This is where most dark 'creator SaaS' sites land; familiar, and glass-on-glow can get muddy and low-contrast in Operate screens.

options.label: Claim & Proof
options.lineage: restrained software marketing: neutral scale, one accent, screenshots as evidence
options.thesis: Navy neutral scale with the logo gradient used a handful of times; every sentence paired with a product screenshot.
options.viewport: Short claim, primary action, large real board screenshot; alternating claim/proof pairs below.
options.case: Strongest on product clarity; weaker on audience identification — it doesn't feel like music.
options.risk: Drifts toward generic if the neon brand is rationed too hard.

options.label: Seven-Segment
options.case: Fuses poorly: a novelty display face, weak identification for most creatives.
options.kept: Unlit states designed as deliberately as lit ones.

options.label: Sliding Planes
options.case: Conflicts with the pinned palette and has no musical identification.
options.kept: Only the moving edge takes colour.

options.label: Glyph Render
options.case: Costume of a terminal; hurts clarity.

options.label: Memory Quilt
options.case: Warm but off-brand against the neon identity.
options.kept: Visible provenance: every item shows who made it.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished dark SaaS dashboard and landing, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Headline, subcopy, two buttons, screenshot, three feature cards.
